dok_rationale: Part (c) requires adjudicating two interpretations by coordinating the boxplot with the dotplot, distinguishing summaries from distribution features, and defending which display answers a decision question; no single calculation determines the response.
stem: The displays show practice-test times, in minutes, for 24 students. Two students interpret the boxplot.\par\smallskip \textbf{Omar:} ``Most students took about 32 minutes---the middle of the box.''\par \textbf{Nia:} ``A boxplot cannot tell us whether most students took about 32 minutes.''
first_take: Who do you trust more, Omar or Nia? Point to one feature in either display.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Read the median and the two quartiles from the boxplot.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In two sentences, describe the dotplot's groups and empty interval. Count how many students took more than 30 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Whose interpretation is better supported? Use a dotplot feature to explain what the boxplot hides. Choose a display for deciding whether more than half the students need over 30 minutes, and defend your choice.

answers.b: There are 12 times from 22--26 minutes and 11 from 38--44, plus one at 55. No values lie between 26 and 38; exactly 12 of 24 students took more than 30 minutes.
answers.c: Nia: no observations are near 32, which lies between the two groups. The boxplot preserves quartiles but hides that gap; treating its median as where most observations gather is a misreading. Choose the dotplot for the coach: 12 of 24, exactly half, took over 30 minutes, so not more than half.

expectedElements.description: Chooses Nia using the empty interval around 32
Explains that quartiles do not reveal the gap or concentration of individual observations
Chooses dotplot and uses 12 of 24 to reject more-than-half over 30

scoringGuide.E: All three elements are correct and linked to this problem. Accept equivalent plain-language reasoning.
scoringGuide.P: At least one element includes a correct evidence-to-reason link, but another is missing or incorrect.
scoringGuide.I: No correct evidence-to-reason link; only a choice, copied numbers, or unsupported statements.

commonMistakes: Treating the median as the most common value; no student took 32 minutes
Calling the empty 27--37 interval a short bar even though the display is a dotplot
Saying a boxplot shows every observation because it shows the minimum and maximum
Calling 55 a formal $1.5\,\mathrm{IQR}$ outlier; the upper fence is $65.25$
Choosing the boxplot for the coach merely because it is more compact
